answer: Each identity must plant and sustain one distinct native willow on an assigned river plot, GPS-tagged below a canyon rim and fed by glacier melt. A rotating inspector photographs it monthly, matching leaf pattern and trunk girth to the prior record, since real growth over 18 months cannot be rushed or copied. 1,000 Sybils need 1,000 leased plots at $70 monthly ($70,000 monthly), seedlings, watering and 18 months of tending, and lose a 5-coin bond per dead or shared tree. Trade-off: admission is slow and favours agents near plantable land.
